newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa surprises market with new high.
newsitem.headline: Absa surprises market with new high.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa powered ahead in Wednesday trade, causing dealers and analysts to wonder, but agreeing that it was a "good buy" and debating that a new deal could be in the pipeline.
Dealers said that while Absa had been attractive for a weeks now, the market seemed only recently to woken up to the fact.

"Absa is one of the favourable banks in the sector. We have been calling it a buy and it looks like it will outperform in the next 18 months. If you want to be overweight in the financial sector then Absa is the share to buy," a dealer said.
Another dealer said: "It is really looking very, very good. It has always been a good stock and the market is now looking at it favourably."
Absa rose 10.89 percent, or 270 cents, to reach a new year high of 27.50 rand before ending 200 cents, or 8.06 percent, up on a volume of 170,900 shares valued at over 4.5 million rand.
An analyst who asked not to be identified said that he had been expecting earnings growth in the mid-20 percent range.
"Unless someone has heard something new, we are looking for earnings growth in the mid-20 percent... I am amazed and I don't know why (it is rising)," he said.
A dealer said the rise indicated that there could be a favourable deal in the pipeline.
"Obviously there is something going on. The volumes are reasonable," one said.
The financial index was hoisted 160 points, or 2.06 percent to 7,988.9 points on the day.
